title: POC scoping - PII & logging constraints for Arcadia BioSolutions
summary: POC-scope call to define success criteria and data handling requirements. Customer (Arcadia BioSolutions) requires strict PII handling: no prompt retention, redaction on ingest, and audit logs in their VPC. Discussed workload sizing (10k seeded prompts, 50k synthetic variations), benchmark targets (80 rps baseline, 95th latency <600ms for 512 tokens), timeline (4-6 week pilot), and artifacts to exchange: security docs, sample config, and benchmark harness. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: PII redaction at ingestion vs post-hoc
logging and audit trails in private deployment
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 summary, private deployment security deck, and sample POC config (Jordan) - by 2025-04-07
Arcadia to provide redacted sample dataset (Priya) - by 2025-04-10
Schedule 1-hour technical onboarding for private VPC install with Arcadia infra team (Sofia/Jordan & Dana) - target week of 2025-04-14
Agree on benchmark harness (scripts, metrics) and test window (2 days) - owners: Sofia + Priya
action_items: Jordan Patel: Send security whitepaper + SOC2 snapshot + network checklist (due 2025-04-07)
Sofia Martinez: Draft POC benchmark harness (JMeter+custom token logger) and example config for 10k prompts (due 2025-04-09)
Priya Rao: Share sample dataset with PII placeholders and acceptance criteria for redaction (due 2025-04-10)
Lena Cho: Provide list of required audit fields for compliance logs (due 2025-04-11)
Mark Rivers: Confirm procurement window and sign-off stakeholders (due 2025-04-15)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Mark (Arcadia CTO), Lena (Sec Eng), Priya (ML), Dana (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Jordan, AE on the account, and Sofia will handle the technical side.
[00:08] Mark: Hi Jordan, hi Sofia. Mark here. We wanted to lock down the POC scope today, specifically around PII and logs.
[00:14] Sofia: Great. Quick agenda — success criteria, dataset and sizing, redaction/retention, benchmarks and timeline. Is that right Dana?
[00:20] Dana: Yes, that's what we need.
[00:22] [00:30] Lena: I'll jump in on the security side. We have strict rules: no persistent storage of raw prompts that may contain patient identifiers; auditability for who queried what; and K M S-backed key management.
[00:40] Jordan: Understood. For the POC options we can do a Redwood Private deployment in your VPC or a dedicated instance in our infra with VPC peering. Since you want keys under your control it sounds like Private is preferable, correct?
[00:51] Mark: Yep, Private preferred. We need to ensure data never leaves our environment.
[01:05] Sofia: Two technical notes up front — 1) we can enable real-time redaction at ingest using our prompt preprocessing hook; that strips or replaces candidate PII and optionally hashes tokens. 2) We can turn off prompt retention at the logging layer so prompts are not persisted to disk, only ephemeral in RAM and optionally hashed for traceability.
[01:22] Priya: Quick question — when you say "turn off retention," does that mean no prompt text is ever stored even for short-term debugging? We need that guarantee for HIPAA alignment.
[01:32] Sofia: By default our console and logs show request bodies for debugging, but in Private you can set the policy to redact request bodies and only store a request hash + metadata. For debugging we can provide a temporary trace mode that requires explicit opt-in and is gated by RBAC.
[01:45] Lena: Can you confirm audit logs still capture who called the API, timestamp, model version, and response status? We need immutable audit trails for compliance.
[01:53] Jordan: Yes, audit logs can be configured to include caller identity (SSO subject), route, model id, tokens consumed and status — without storing full prompt text.
[02:05] [02:30] Mark: On workload sizing. We plan to seed the POC with 10k real conversations and generate ~50k synthetic perturbations for load. Target baseline is around 80 requests per second, with spikes to 150 rps for short windows. Latency goal is P95 <600ms for up to 512 tokens context. Thoughts?
[02:50] Sofia: That sizing is reasonable. For 80 rps sustained with 512 token inputs we recommend Dedicated GPUs in the private cluster with 3 worker nodes for headroom. If spikes to 150 occur we can burst to an additional pool if you enable autoscale.
[03:05] Priya: And memory of KV cache — do cached prefixes persist across requests? We don't want any sensitive prefix state to be retained between sessions.
[03:13] Sofia: KV cache is in-memory per worker and is not durable. For the POC we can configure it to flush at session boundaries and also encrypt the cache in RAM using the host's memory encryption where available.
[03:25] [03:45] Lena: Encryption at rest is mandatory. Also need KMS integration — HSM or cloud KMS is fine as long as keys are customer-managed.
[03:53] Jordan: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and customer-managed keys for Private. HSM via CloudHSM or equivalent is supported in the network design.
[04:05] Sofia: One subtlety — embeddings. If you call the embeddings API we often recommend an opt-in to retention for index building; for this POC, you said you do not want any stored embeddings, right?
[04:15] Mark: Correct. All embeddings generated during the POC must be ephemeral. If we need to index, we'll use a separate, on-prem vector DB that we control.
[04:24] Sofia: Perfect — we can disable the embedding-store feature for your tenant during the pilot.
[04:30] [04:50] Dana: Success criteria from product perspective: 1) PII redaction efficacy (false negatives <1% on the test set), 2) Latency/Throughput targets met, 3) No retention of prompts or embeddings, 4) Audit logs accessible to security team.
[05:05] Jordan: We'll codify those as measurable checks in the benchmark harness. Sofia will provide the harness and an expected test plan.
[05:13] [05:30] Sofia: Regarding benchmarks — we'll run two phases: functional redaction accuracy, then load/latency tests. For redaction we need a labeled set (Priya to supply 2k labeled examples with PII marks). For load tests we'll run a 2-day window: steady-state for 4 hours at 80 rps, then spike tests up to 150 rps for short bursts. We'll capture P50/P95/P99 latencies, error rates, and tokens/sec.
[05:55] Priya: For labeling we can do 2k examples and flag patient ids, phone numbers, and account IDs. We'll include obfuscated examples too to see false positives.
[06:05] [06:30] Mark: Timeline — can we get the POC running in ~4 weeks? Our procurement window is tight; we want technical results to influence a Q2 decision.
[06:40] Jordan: Typical POC timeline: week 0 prep (network, keys, config), week 1 install and onboarding, week 2 functional redaction and small scale tests, week 3 full-scale benchmarks, week 4 wrap + report. That's 4 weeks if procurement and infra are ready. If procurement delays, it can extend to 6.
[06:58] Lena: What kind of SLA or uptime does Redwood offer for the private POC cluster? We need guidance for if a worker crash causes state loss.
[07:08] Sofia: For POC we don't typically offer enterprise SLA but we design nodes with redundancy. If you want SLA-like guarantees we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity; however in Private we can set up multi-az workers and fault-tolerant routing.
[07:24] [07:45] Dana: A few compliance items — SSO/SAML for user access, RBAC control for trace mode, encryption in transit and at rest, and log retention policy (we want logs retained for 90 days but no raw prompts).
[07:58] Jordan: All doable. You can configure log retention separately for audit logs (90 days) and debug traces (disabled by default).
[08:10] [08:30] Priya: About prompt hashing — is there an out-of-the-box way to store only a salted hash of prompt text for deduping and traceability?
[08:40] Sofia: Yes — we support salted hashing where the salt is customer-provided. Hashes can be stored in audit logs instead of raw text. That allows you to identify duplicates without seeing raw prompts.
[08:53] Lena: Need to ensure hashes cannot be reversed or correlated to small known inputs. We'll want to review the hash algorithm and salt management.
[09:00] Jordan: We'll include the hashing details in the security docs we send.
[09:08] [09:30] Mark: Any limitations on model variants or quantization? We want to test a few mid-sized open models for cost/perf tradeoffs.
[09:40] Sofia: We can stage two model variants for the POC: a medium open model (quantized int8) and a larger variant. We’ll instrument costs and compare token/sec and latency. Note: quantization can slightly alter generation fuzziness so we'll include quality checks.
closing_notes: Recap: Redwood to share security artifacts and POC config; Arcadia to provide datasets and audit requirements. Target private deployment in VPC, 4-week POC with redaction and no prompt retention, benchmark harness to be agreed. Next meeting scheduled during onboarding week once procurement confirmed.
notes_timestamped: [10:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc bundle. [10:05] Mark: Appreciate it. [10:07] Call ended.
